## Test Execution Flow
``` Test Execution Flow ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ Test Runner (Maven) │ │ mvn test │ └──────────┬──────────────────┘ ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Test Discovery & Execution │ │ ├─ Discovers @Test annotated methods │ │ ├─ Runs @Parameterized tests with each parameter set │ │ └─ Executes tests in JUnit runner │ └──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ↓ ┌─────┴─────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ┌────────┐ ┌────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ │ Setup │ │ Execution │ │ Assertions │ │ Teardown │ │(Before)│ │ (Test) │ │ (Verify) │ │ (After) │ └───┬────┘ └────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬──────┘ │ │ │ │ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ Given() When() Then() Report ├─Spec ├─Method ├─Status ✓ Pass ├─Headers ├─Endpoint ├─Content-Type ✗ Fail ├─Body └─Query Params ├─Body Fields ⊘ Skip └─Auth ├─Data Values ├─Types └─Consistency ```

## Test Data Flow - Creating & Validating a Visit
``` Create Visit Test Flow ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 1. BUILD REQUEST DATA │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ Input: date="2026-06-07", desc="Test", petId=1 │ │ ↓ │ │ VisitTestHelper.buildVisitJson() │ │ ↓ │ │ JSON Output: │ │ { │ │ "date": "2026-06-07", │ │ "description": "Test", │ │ "petId": 1 │ │ } │ │ │ └────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘ ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 2. SEND HTTP REQUEST │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ given() │ │ .spec(requestSpec) │ │ .header("Content-Type", "application/json") │ │ .body(json) │ │ .when() │ │ .post("/visits") │ │ │ │ HTTP: POST /visits HTTP/1.1 │ │ Content-Type: application/json │ │ Body: { "date": "2026-06-07", ... } │ │ │ └────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘ ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 3. RECEIVE & PARSE RESPONSE │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ HTTP/1.1 201 Created │ │ Content-Type: application/json │ │ │ │ { │ │ "id": 42, │ │ "date": "2026-06-07", │ │ "description": "Test", │ │ "petId": 1 │ │ } │ │ │ └────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘ ↓ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 4. VALIDATE RESPONSE │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ .then() │ │ .statusCode(201) ✓ Correct HTTP 201 │ │ .contentType("application/json") ✓ Is JSON │ │ .body("id", notNullValue()) ✓ Has id │ │ .body("id", greaterThan(0)) ✓ Valid id │ │ .body("date", equalTo("2026-06-07")) ✓ Data match │ │ .body("description", equalTo("Test")) ✓ Data match │ │ .body("petId", equalTo(1)) ✓ Data match │ │ │ │ Result: ✓ PASS - All assertions passed │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ```

## Response Assertion Strategy
``` Assertion Layers - Progressive Validation ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Layer 1: HTTP Response Metadata ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ .statusCode(201) │ │ .contentType("application/json") │ │ │ ✓ Confirms: Request succeeded │ │ ✓ Confirms: Response is JSON │ └───────────────────────────────┘ ↓
Layer 2: Response Structure ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ │ .body("$", hasKey("id")) │ │ .body("$", hasKey("date")) │ │ .body("$", hasKey("description")) │ .body("$", hasKey("petId")) │ │ │ │ ✓ Confirms: All required fields │ │ ✓ Confirms: No missing fields │ └─────────────────────────────────┘ ↓
Layer 3: Field Data Types ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ .body("id", isA(Integer.class)) │ .body("date", isA(String.class)) │ │ │ ✓ Confirms: Correct types │ │ ✓ Confirms: Serialization OK │ └──────────────────────────────┘ ↓
Layer 4: Field Values ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ │ .body("id", greaterThan(0)) │ │ .body("date", equalTo("2026-06-07")) │ .body("description", equalTo("Test")) │ │ │ ✓ Confirms: Values are correct │ │ ✓ Confirms: Business logic OK │ └─────────────────────────────────┘ ↓
Layer 5: Value Constraints ┌───────────────────────────────────┐ │ .body("date", │ │ matchesPattern("\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")) │ .body("id", greaterThan(0)) │ │ │ │ ✓ Confirms: Data format correct │ │ ✓ Confirms: Business constraints │ └───────────────────────────────────┘ ```

START │ ↓ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Request Valid? │ └────┬────────┬───┘ YES NO │ │ ↓ ↓ Process ┌─────────────────────┐ Request │ What's the problem? │ │ └────┬────┬────┬────┬──┘ │ │ │ │ │ │ ┌─┴──────────┼──┼──┤ │ │ │ Resource │ Missing Body-Parse Auth │ Exist? │ Fields Error Error └┬─────────┬─┘ │ │ │ YES NO │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ┌──────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌───┐┌──────────┐ │ Success? │ │ 404 │ │400││ 400 │ └──┬───┬───┘ │Not │ │Bad││Unsupported YES NO │Found │ │Req││ Media │ │ │ └────────┘ │ ││ Type │ ↓ ↓ └───┘└──────────┘ ┌──────┐ └─────────────────┘ ┌────┤ 200 │ │ │ OK │ │ └──────┘ │ ├─ Success with body? → 200 OK ✓ ├─ Success no body? → 204 No Content ✓ ├─ Created resource? → 201 Created ✓ └─ Validation error? → 400 Bad Request ✓ ```

## Best Practices Checklist
``` ✓ Implemented Best Practices ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
API Test Design: ✓ One assertion focus per test ✓ Descriptive test method names ✓ Happy path + error cases tested ✓ Edge cases and boundary conditions ✓ Parameterized tests for multiple scenarios ✓ Tests are independent and repeatable ✓ No hardcoded IDs (create first, then use) ✓ Proper HTTP status code expectations
Assertions: ✓ Status code validation ✓ Content-Type validation ✓ Response structure validation ✓ Field existence validation ✓ Field type validation ✓ Field value validation ✓ Constraint validation ✓ Error message validation
Code Quality: ✓ DRY principle (Don't Repeat Yourself) ✓ Helper classes for common operations ✓ Meaningful variable names ✓ Proper code organization ✓ Comments where needed ✓ No unused code/methods ✓ Consistent formatting ✓ Single responsibility per method
Test Structure: ✓ Clear test organization by endpoint ✓ Separation of basic vs advanced tests ✓ Logical grouping of related tests ✓ Easy to find and maintain ✓ Scalable architecture ✓ Easy to extend for new endpoints
Maintenance: ✓ Changes in one place only (helpers) ✓ Easy to add new test cases ✓ Easy to update API endpoints ✓ Self-documenting code ✓ Clear documentation provided ✓ Examples for other APIs ```

Phase 2: Apply to Other Endpoints (Recommended) ├─ Owner API Tests │ ├─ OwnerAPITest.java (Refactored) │ ├─ OwnerAPITestAdvanced.java (Edge cases) │ └─ OwnerAPITestHelper.java (Utilities) ├─ Pet API Tests │ ├─ PetAPITest.java (Refactored) │ ├─ PetAPITestAdvanced.java (Edge cases) │ └─ PetAPITestHelper.java (Utilities) ├─ Specialty API Tests └─ Total: 150-200 tests
